events.statement: The accident under investigation was a ceiling collapse in the connector tunnel to the Ted Williams Tunnel in Boston, Massachusetts.

quotes.quote: Date : July 10, 2006
Vehicle : Connector Tunnel to Ted Williams Tunnel

events.statement: NTSB's Materials Laboratory Division issued Report No. 06-090 documenting torque-versus-axial-load tests on simulated ceiling anchor assemblies.

quotes.quote: December 7, 2006
Report No. 06-090

events.statement: Torque versus axial load tests were run on simulated anchor assemblies, using hardware recovered from the failure location, at FHWA's Turner Fairbank Highway Research Center.

quotes.quote: On October 10, and October 31, 2006, torque versus axial load tests were performed on simulated anchor assemblies at the Federal Highway Administration’s Turner Fairbank Highway Research Center.

events.statement: MCC's surveying crew began laying out the locations for drilling the ceiling anchor holes in the I-90 eastbound tunnel.

quotes.quote: The Contractor's surveying crew began laying out the locations for drilling holes in the ceiling of the I-90 E BD ceiling, C04A2 contract area.

events.statement: Field engineers observed a prototype core drilling of holes for the ceiling support anchor bolts, with a Hilti representative present for technical assistance.

quotes.quote: MOBILIZATION: At 09:15 FArch Barrett & FE McCrabb reported to the east end of I-90 EB at the portal area to observe prototype core drilling of holes for ceiling support anchor bolts.
Pete Sullivan of Hilti (core drill supplier, ph= 800-879-8000) was also there for technical assistance.

events.statement: A magnetic survey of ceiling anchor bolt holes found that many holes MCC had reported as clear of rebar actually contained severed rebar.

quotes.quote: Magnetic inspection reveiled 32 of those locations did, in fact, contain steel re-bar which had been severed.

events.statement: MCC proposed filling abandoned ceiling anchor holes with epoxy instead of non-shrink grout, and the field engineer asked MCC to submit an RFI on the change.

quotes.quote: S. Abbotts (MCC) stated that they intend to use epoxy to fill abandoned anchor bolt holes rather than the non-shrink grout. FArch requested they submit an RFI.

events.statement: Ceiling anchor bolts were being installed in the HOV bore without the screens or the compressed-air hole blow-out called for in the epoxy manufacturer's installation instructions.

quotes.quote: The bolts were installed without screens to hold the epoxy, and without blowing the holes out w/ compressed air per Manufacturer's recommendations.

events.statement: CONAM Inspection Inc. began pull-out load testing of the new ceiling anchor bolts in the HOV mock-up area; 3 of the first 36 bolts tested failed.

quotes.quote: Representatives of 'CONAM Inspection Inc.' began testing at 8:00, using an Enerpac P-142 (Ser # S10420) hydraulic tester. A total of 36 bolts were tested and there were 3 failures.

events.statement: Field engineers found that bolts attaching angle brackets to the precast wall panels were not stainless steel, though the receiving inserts were; MCC's Jim Martin said the panels would go up with the bolts on hand and be changed later.

quotes.quote: The bolts attaching the angle brackets to the top of the pre-cast wall panels were not stainless steel.
When pointed out to MCC's Jim Martin they said they would have to put up the panels with what they had and change the bolts at a later date.

events.statement: CONAM Inspection technicians pull-out tested ceiling anchor bolts in the HOV and EB bores and found further failures, including a bolt that passed the load test but was seen to turn.

quotes.quote: There were two technicians from Conam Inspection Inc performing anchor bolt pull out tests in the HOV and in EB. In HOV, 4 bolts were tested and there were two failures.

events.statement: Ironworkers found hanger support assembly bolts that were short and missing locking devices, shim washers, and gaskets on ceiling modules HOV078 and HOV079; the issue was reported to MCC's J. Martin as a potential deficiency.

quotes.quote: Note: (1.5 in Dia.) hanger support assembly bolts short.missing locking DEVICE & shim washers On subject Bolt are Short.missing gaskets between precast ceiling panels (HOV078;HOV079)
J.martin NOTIFIED & these items will be corrected.Reported potential Deficiency Ref.DTL.20 Dwg.#S-276;S-349;Spec.723.480-1.02A.

events.statement: MCC and B/PB met with Powers Fasteners' field engineering manager to determine the cause of the pull-out of 5 ceiling anchors in the HOV078 mock-up module; Powers Fasteners was identified as the manufacturer of the epoxy used to install the stainless-steel ceiling anchors.

quotes.quote: The subject of the meeting was to discuss and determine the cause of the pull out of 5 of the ceiling anchors in the mock-up at ceiling module HOV078.
It should be noted that Powers Fasteners is the manufacturer of the epoxy used to install the 5/8" stainless steel ceiling anchors.

events.statement: CONAM Inspection technicians pull-out tested 40 ceiling anchor bolts in the EB and WB bores of the 4A2 area and found one failure, while ironworkers continued hanging precast ceiling modules.

quotes.quote: There were two technicians from Conam Inspection Inc. performing ceiling anchor bolt pull out tests in the EB and WB bores of the 4A2 area. They tested a total of 40 bolts, and there was one failure.

events.statement: Laborers drilled and installed adhesive anchor bolts in the EB bore at locations where ceiling hanger plates could not be mounted on the existing Unistrut, staying late so the bolts could be pull-tested before ceiling hanging resumed.

quotes.quote: Two laborers were drilling and installing adhesive anchor bolts in the EB bore at approx Sta 68+00 at locations where the ceiling hanger plates could not be mounted in existing Unistrut.

events.statement: B/PB issued Deficiency Report No. 1, finding that at least five ceiling adhesive anchors in the area of ceiling module HOV 079 had pulled out since the module was hung.

quotes.quote: DATE ISSUED: December 1, 1999
At least five ceiling adhesive anchors in the area of ceiling module HOV 079 have failed, that is pull-out has been observed, since the hanging of the ceiling module

events.statement: MCC disputed B/PB's position that an approved submittal's manufacturer data on a 6350 lb bond strength had become a contract requirement overriding the original 3250 lb specification for adhesive anchor testing under CP #22.

quotes.quote: January 19, 2000

an approved submittal including manufacturer’s data denoting an allowable adhesive bond strength of 6350 lbs now becomes a contract “requirement”, taking precedence over the original contract specification value of 3250 lbs.

events.statement: Retesting of adhesive anchor bolts to the higher 6350-lb criterion found two bolts that held the load when first applied but 'popped' loose during the required two-minute hold, coming out of the hole almost clean of cured epoxy.

quotes.quote: The testing procedure requires the load to be held for two minutes. During the two minute holding period both bolts 'popped' loose.
Both bolts came out almost perfectly clean, with almost no sign of cured epoxy clinging to either one.

events.statement: B/PB closed Deficiency Report No. 1, noting that all HOV ceiling anchor bolts had been retested to the new criteria and that failures had been replaced and retested.

quotes.quote: January 26, 2001
All HOV A/B Retested to new criteria, failures have been replaced & Retested

open_questions: Whether the anchors examined in NTSB Materials Laboratory Report 06-090 (labeled 3-3, 3-32, 5-1, 5-2, 5-22, 6-1) are from the same HOV ceiling section whose 1999-2000 pull-out failures and clean epoxy release are documented in the C09B2 daily reports and Deficiency Report No. 1.
Whether Deficiency Report No. 1 (closed January 2001, retested to a higher load criterion) covered all ceiling anchors in the tunnel or only those in the HOV mock-up area it names.
